title: CO2 removal scaling for Mars-duration missions
bottleneck: The ISS scrubs CO2 with systems sized for low Earth orbit and regular resupply of sorbent materials; a Mars transit vehicle and surface habitat need larger, more reliable, fully regenerable CO2 removal running for years without spare parts. Amine swing beds degrade, zeolite systems need high regeneration temperatures, and all consume significant power and reject heat. Pairing CO2 removal with oxygen recovery adds complexity: the loop must balance continuously or the atmosphere drifts.
why_it_blocks: CO2 above about 1 percent impairs cognition and can kill; the removal system is as life-critical as oxygen supply, and Mars architectures assume it just works for 1,000 days straight.
current_state: The ISS Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly has a checkered reliability history; four-bed molecular sieve and thermal amine systems are in development for Orion and Gateway. Mars-duration reliability is unproven.
